title: Roberto Acciaiuoli to the Signoria from Amiens, 23 October 1513: Bourbon to Burgundy, the king's anger and the English embarkation (catalogue 2351)

documents.shelfmark: Archivio di Stato di Firenze, Mediceo avanti il Principato, filza LXXII, doc. 192 (old c. 234), recto and verso
documents.route: Roberto Acciaiuoli, Florentine orator at the French court (Amiens) to the Signoria (Magnifici viri)

plaintext.source: No decipherment of doc. 192 found. Docs. 190 and 191 of the same filza are a cipher letter of the same day and its contemporary clear copy.

transcription.source: Claude from ASF images 79574 and 79575 (1272 px), with the key in hand; two blind passes over the whole letter and two over thirteen lines by further Claude instances; reviewed by Codex.

system.summary: Consonant sign with the vowel as a superscript figure (1-5 = u, o, i, e, a), bare letter signs with homophones, doubled-consonant signs, word signs, and numbers as code words.

diacritics.note: The superscript figure is the vowel.

system.sibling_key: Same system as pandolfini1514 (Brice Dudout's key v6). Acciaiuoli's own cipher is Gabbrielli's key no. 120 (DECODE R5807).

prior_solution.where: Catalogue 2351 vetting (Canestrini vol. II) and a search of Desjardins-Canestrini vol. II and Sanudo vol. XVII found no decipherment or edition of doc. 192.

conditions.human_role: Andrew Aymeloglu requested the investigation, the second-model review and the submission.

solution.what: Codex applies Dudout's pandolfini1514 key v6 to a first transcription and reads the Bourbon passage.
Claude re-transcribes both faces from enlarged line strips with the key in hand; two fresh instances make blind passes from shape names alone.
Doc. 190 aligned sign by sign against its clear copy 191; corrections fitted on nine lines, 84-94% agreement on 93 held-out signs whose clear word was read before decoding.
Reading with v6 plus the 190/191 values: 85% of signs. A sign count including bracketed corrections was first reported as 96% of words, which overstated it.

Second blind round on the thirteen hardest lines from tighter crops; signs both readers agree on are adopted. Opens V8-10 and clauses at V1, V5, R6, R12. The number 26 read at R12 is withdrawn, then restored with a query after review.
Gabbrielli's key no. 120 for Acciaioli found on DECODE (R5807) and transcribed: confirms the values and 22 = Lanzichinecchi, corrects se to quando, adds quanto, ora, tanto, galee.

Codex reviews the reading against the manuscript and key images: strict word count 86-90%, not 96%; corrects nientedimeno, perché, facto, passaggio; asks for queries on supplied words. Applied where confirmed on crops; status set to read in part.
Gabbrielli's keys no. 89 and no. 111 for Acciaioli checked for the numbers 15, 26, 47: both are different ciphers.

outcome.method: key recovered based on plaintext from external sources
outcome.method_basis: The system was recognised from Dudout's pandolfini1514 key; the values were then fixed by the 190/191 cipher and clear pair of the same day and confirmed by Gabbrielli's nineteenth-century reconstruction of Acciaioli's cipher (no. 120), which is independent of this letter. Values resting on this letter alone are marked 192 in key.tsv.
outcome.fraction_read_source: reading-it.md, cipher words: 692 of about 770 read from the signs with nothing supplied; 21 more carry a supplied letter, 30 are proposed words marked [?word], 25 are unread (sizes estimated from the number of signs), 2 are the unidentified number 15. Elided forms counted as two words.

texts.summary: Louis XII has ordered Bourbon into Burgundy with lances and Landsknechte; news of a rout has overturned a plan; the king is angry at people who yielded to the English; the English king embarks at Calais; the king says he is secure and will fight if the Swiss move; the prelates leave for Rome after All Saints.
texts.note: 192-literal.txt is the unedited output of key.tsv. The reading departs from it at the 23 places of 192-repairs.tsv and wherever it prints brackets. read_share counts words read with nothing supplied.

gaps.item: 25 unread words (R5, V1, V5, V13, V14-15 and single words)
gaps.detail: superscript vowels not separable at the 1272 px of the public images
the signs as transcribed do not spell them; mostly one vowel or one consonant off
not in Gabbrielli's key no. 120; 15 proposed as the Venetians from Sanudo
